newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Weak bullion dogs Zimbabwe's marginal gold mines.
newsitem.headline: Weak bullion dogs Zimbabwe's marginal gold mines.

text.p: The current soft bullion price is threatening Zimbabwe's marginal gold mines and stunting the industry's expansion, the Chamber of Mines said on Monday.

Derek Bain, chief executive of the mining industry's representative body, told Reuters that the weak gold price -- last bid at $340.90 an ounce -- had hurled a number of high-cost, low-output mines into loss.
"The price of gold could put marginal mines in difficulty. At the moment there are mines operating at a loss," he said.
Bain did not expand on what these mines were.
Asked about whether the industry hoped to expand on its 1996 gold production of 24.7 tonnes, Bain said,"At this particular point in time no-one is looking at anything."
"The mining potential is excellent but at the moment is totally handicapped by prices," he added.
Numerous and large exploration programmes are underway in Zimbabwe and, subject to prices, the industry is "poised for growth", he said.
Bain said silver, platinum and base metal production is also being hit by weak prices in those minerals.
"Prices on the LME (London Metal Exchange) are literally bouncing up and down like a yo-yo. How can you judge anything on that?" he said.
